segments.t: On macOS, use KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003 where KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 is shown.

These are the default shortcuts. You can give most commands of the menus other keys, remove a shortcut or give a command without one a shortcut in KTPH006Settings → KeyboardKTPH007; the menus and the command palette always show the shortcut in effect. KTPH008CutKTPH009, KTPH010CopyKTPH011, KTPH012PasteKTPH013, KTPH014Previous PromptKTPH015, KTPH016Next PromptKTPH017, the zoom keys, KTPH018KTPH000KTPH019, KTPH020KTPH001KTPH021+KTPH022KTPH002KTPH023, KTPH024KTPH003KTPH025+KTPH026KTPH004KTPH027+KTPH028KTPH005KTPH029 and the tab jump keys stay fixed.

Open or close the KTPH000command paletteKTPH001 to find and run any menu command by name, run a KTPH002terminal or tab commandKTPH003 such as KTPH004Clear BufferKTPH005, KTPH006switch to an open tabKTPH007, KTPH008connect to a saved connectionKTPH009 or KTPH010run a snippetKTPH011 (also while a terminal has the focus)
Reopen the last closed terminal tab (also while a terminal has the focus)
Next Tab (KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 on macOS too); with KTPH003most-recently-used orderKTPH004 on, the tab used before the current one
Previous Tab (KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 on macOS too); with most-recently-used order on, the tab used longest ago
Jump to the first to eighth tab of the window (top row or numpad)
Jump to the last tab of the window
Find in the active tab (in a focused terminal on Windows and Linux the key goes to the shell, see KTPH000TerminalKTPH001)

Quick Select: label the web addresses, paths, e-mail addresses, IP addresses, hashes and numbers the focused terminal pane shows, to copy one or open it with a key (terminal tabs only), see KTPH000Quick selectKTPH001
Manage credentials (also while a terminal has the focus)
Start / stop the session journal of the active tab
Add a screenshot to the running session journal
Show/hide the live journal panel on its last-used side
Show/hide the Coding Agents panel on its last-used side
Jump to the next coding agent waiting for a decision, across windows
Dock the file browser on the left
Dock the file browser on the right
Zoom the terminal font in/out (Cmd + wheel on macOS)
Close a local cmd.exe/PowerShell tab (EOF for bash-family shells and SSH)
Switch KTPH000keyword highlightingKTPH001 on or off for the focused terminal pane

The zoom keys (KTPH008KTPH000KTPH009 or KTPH010KTPH001KTPH011 with KTPH012KTPH002KTPH013 / KTPH014KTPH003KTPH015 / KTPH016KTPH004KTPH017; KTPH018KTPH005KTPH019 on macOS) zoom the terminal only while a terminal tab is selected. In a snippet editor or file editor tab they reach the editor, and KTPH020KTPH006KTPH021+KTPH022KTPH007KTPH023 types its character there.

The tab jump keys work in every tab, also while a terminal or an editor has the focus, and a number with no tab at its position does nothing. On macOS they are KTPH019KTPH000KTPH020 with a digit, and KTPH021KTPH001KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH002KTPH024 with a digit works too, so a French (AZERTY) Mac can reach its digits (macOS keeps KTPH025KTPH003KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH004KTPH028+KTPH029KTPH005KTPH030 to KTPH031KTPH006KTPH032+KTPH033KTPH007KTPH034+KTPH035KTPH008KTPH036 for screenshots). On Windows and Linux they are exactly KTPH037KTPH009KTPH038 with a digit: KTPH039KTPH010KTPH040 combinations (which arrive as KTPH041KTPH011KTPH042+KTPH043KTPH012KTPH044) and KTPH045KTPH013KTPH046+KTPH047KTPH014KTPH048+KTPH049KTPH015KTPH050 (the Cisco break sequence) still reach the terminal. A digit key that types KTPH051KTPH016KTPH052 or KTPH053KTPH017KTPH054 in your layout, such as the AZERTY 6 key, stays a zoom key instead. On Linux with a layout whose number row types other characters, the top-row digits may not jump; the numpad digits (with KTPH055KTPH018KTPH056 on) do.

KTPH011KTPH000KTPH012+KTPH013KTPH001KTPH014 and KTPH015KTPH002KTPH016+KTPH017KTPH003KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH004KTPH020 follow the tab bar unless KTPH021Ctrl+Tab switches tabs in the order they were last usedKTPH022 is on in the KTPH023Window settingsKTPH024. Then KTPH025KTPH005KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH006KTPH028 goes back to the tab you used before the current one; keep KTPH029KTPH007KTPH030 held and press KTPH031KTPH008KTPH032 again to go further back, add KTPH033KTPH009KTPH034 to step the other way, and release KTPH035KTPH010KTPH036 at the tab you want. Only that tab counts as used. Any other key ends the step-through first and then acts on the tab you stopped at.

Reopen Closed Tab uses KTPH017KTPH001KTPH018+KTPH019KTPH002KTPH020+KTPH021KTPH003KTPH022+KTPH023KTPH004KTPH024 because KTPH025KTPH005KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH006KTPH028+KTPH029KTPH007KTPH030 toggles the command timestamps and KTPH031KTPH008KTPH032+KTPH033KTPH009KTPH034+KTPH035KTPH010KTPH036 the session journal. On Windows, KTPH037KTPH011KTPH038 arrives as KTPH039KTPH012KTPH040+KTPH041KTPH013KTPH042, so on a layout where KTPH043KTPH014KTPH044+KTPH045KTPH015KTPH046+KTPH047KTPH016KTPH048 types a character (such as KTPH000 on US-International) that combination reopens a closed tab instead, and the character is not typed.
These keys work while a terminal pane has the focus. For how they behave with several panes, see KTPH000Broadcast modeKTPH001.
Copy the terminal selection / paste into the terminal (Windows and Linux; KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007 / KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 on macOS)
Paste into the terminal; on Linux KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003+KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 goes to the shell
Sent to the shell: redraws or clears the screen in bash, psql or a REPL, and the scrollback is kept
Sent to the shell: moves the cursor one character forward at a bash prompt and pages forward in KTPH000 or KTPH001
Clear Buffer: empty the terminal screen and its scrollback
Back-tab (KTPH000), for example to go back one field or panel in a full-screen program
Move one word left / right in the shell (Windows and Linux)
Move one word left / right on macOS (sends KTPH000 / KTPH001, as Terminal.app does)
Scroll korTTY's scrollback by a page; inside a full-screen program such as KTPH000, KTPH001 or KTPH002 the key goes to the program

Scroll korTTY's scrollback by a line (KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007 / KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 on macOS); on Windows and Linux the keys go to a full-screen program instead while one runs

Jump to the previous / next prompt (KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 / KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on macOS) in a pane whose shell is set up for KTPH018shell integrationKTPH019; in a pane without prompt marks, and while a full-screen program runs, the keys reach the program as before
Next / previous tab, also while the terminal has the focus (the KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 key on macOS too)
Jump to a tab, also while the terminal has the focus (KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 on macOS, see KTPH003GeneralKTPH004)
Reopen the last closed terminal tab, also while the terminal has the focus (KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 on macOS)

Open the link in the browser or mail program (KTPH002KTPH001KTPH003 + click on macOS), also a web or e-mail address printed as plain text; a file path or KTPH000 link opens as text in the Snippet Editor in SSH and local-shell tabs; a plain click on a link does nothing, and right-click → KTPH004Open LinkKTPH005 or KTPH006Open File in Snippet EditorKTPH007 works without the key, see KTPH008Links in terminal outputKTPH009
a label's letters / KTPH001KTPH000KTPH002 + the last letter (while quick select runs)

Copy the labelled text / open a web or e-mail address, or a file path in the Snippet Editor; KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003 takes back the first letter of a two-letter label, KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 or any other key ends quick select, see KTPH006Quick selectKTPH007

On Windows and Linux, KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007 to KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011 no longer reach the program in the terminal: korTTY's terminal never sent them as keys of their own, so no program loses a binding it could receive.

On Windows and Linux, KTPH021Clear BufferKTPH022 and KTPH023FindKTPH024 have no key of their own, so KTPH025KTPH002KTPH026+KTPH027KTPH003KTPH028 and KTPH029KTPH004KTPH030+KTPH031KTPH005KTPH032 stay with the programs running in the terminal. Use right-click → KTPH033Clear BufferKTPH034 or KTPH035FindKTPH036 in the terminal, KTPH037Edit → Find…KTPH038 with the mouse, or reach both from the keyboard through the KTPH039command paletteKTPH040: KTPH041KTPH006KTPH042+KTPH043KTPH007KTPH044+KTPH045KTPH008KTPH046, type KTPH000 or KTPH001, KTPH047KTPH009KTPH048. KTPH049KTPH010KTPH050+KTPH051KTPH011KTPH052+KTPH053KTPH012KTPH054 stays Terminal-only Fullscreen and KTPH055KTPH013KTPH056+KTPH057KTPH014KTPH058+KTPH059KTPH015KTPH060 still docks the file browser on the left. KTPH061KTPH016KTPH062+KTPH063KTPH017KTPH064+KTPH065KTPH018KTPH066 switches keyword highlighting and does not reach the terminal, while plain KTPH067KTPH019KTPH068+KTPH069KTPH020KTPH070 still reaches the shell as backspace.

In that dialog KTPH008CancelKTPH009 is the default button, so KTPH010KTPH000KTPH011, KTPH012KTPH001KTPH013 and KTPH014KTPH002KTPH015 drop the paste; click KTPH016PasteKTPH017, or press KTPH018KTPH003KTPH019 to reach it and KTPH020KTPH004KTPH021 to press it. Every other combination of KTPH024KTPH006KTPH025, KTPH026KTPH007KTPH027 and KTPH028KTPH008KTPH029 with the arrow keys, KTPH030KTPH009KTPH031 / KTPH032KTPH010KTPH033, KTPH034KTPH011KTPH035 / KTPH036KTPH012KTPH037, KTPH038KTPH013KTPH039 / KTPH040KTPH014KTPH041 and KTPH042KTPH015KTPH043 to KTPH044KTPH016KTPH045 is sent the way xterm sends it (KTPH046KTPH017KTPH047 always toggles fullscreen, and in a tab with two or more panes KTPH048KTPH018KTPH049+KTPH050KTPH019KTPH051 with an arrow key moves the focus to another pane instead, see KTPH052PanesKTPH053), for example KTPH054KTPH020KTPH055+KTPH056KTPH021KTPH057 as KTPH000 and KTPH058KTPH022KTPH059+KTPH060KTPH023KTPH061 as KTPH001. These keys split the active terminal tab, move the keyboard focus between its panes and zoom one of them; see KTPH000Split operationsKTPH001.

Split the focused pane on that pane's own server: to the right when the pane is wide, below it when it is tall; the new pane gets the focus (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008 on macOS)
Move the focus to the pane on the left / right (KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 / KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on macOS)
Move the focus to the pane above / below (KTPH006KTPH000KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH001KTPH009+KTPH010KTPH002KTPH011 / KTPH012KTPH003KTPH013+KTPH014KTPH004KTPH015+KTPH016KTPH005KTPH017 on macOS)
Zoom the focused pane so it fills the tab, or show all panes again (KTPH003KTPH000KTPH004+KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008 on macOS)

The split key works in every terminal tab while the keyboard is in it. On Windows and Linux it no longer reaches the shell, which received it as KTPH005KTPH001KTPH006+KTPH007KTPH002KTPH008; KTPH009KTPH003KTPH010+KTPH011KTPH004KTPH012 itself still does, so KTPH000 still saves with it.

The focus keys and the zoom key act only while a terminal tab with two or more panes is active and the keyboard is in that tab; with a single pane they reach the program in the terminal as before, KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005+KTPH006KTPH001KTPH007+KTPH008KTPH002KTPH009 as KTPH010KTPH003KTPH011. At the edge of the tab the focus stays where it is. When several panes lie on that side, the focus goes to the one that lies beside the focused pane rather than only touching its corner, and among those to the nearest one. Moving the focus while a pane is zoomed shows all panes again. KTPH012View → PanesKTPH013 has the same commands, KTPH014Split RightKTPH015 and KTPH016Split DownKTPH017 to choose the side of a split, KTPH018Close PaneKTPH019, KTPH020Zoom PaneKTPH021, and KTPH022Next PaneKTPH023 and KTPH024Previous PaneKTPH025, which go through all panes of the tab and start over after the last one. The KTPH026command paletteKTPH027 runs every one of them by name, and its rows show the keys of the table above.
A desktop shortcut can take these keys first

Some Linux desktops, such as GNOME, Xfce and Cinnamon, switch workspaces with KTPH002KTPH000KTPH003+KTPH004KTPH001KTPH005 and an arrow key, and some Windows graphics drivers (Intel) rotate the screen with it, before korTTY sees the key. Use KTPH006View → PanesKTPH007 there, or switch off the desktop's shortcut.
These keys work while the KTPH000command paletteKTPH001 is open. Every other key stays in the palette and never reaches the terminal behind it.
Close the palette and run the chosen row, or the first row when none is chosen
